source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hand hygiene is not required after leaving because the nurse did not touch the patient directly.","B":"Hand hygiene is indicated after touching equipment in the patient’s immediate surroundings, even without direct patient contact.","C":"Hand hygiene is needed after equipment contact when the device is visibly soiled, but routine contact alone does not create an indication.","D":"Hand hygiene can be deferred until the next patient-care task because no body-fluid exposure occurred."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC hand-hygiene guidance includes performing hand hygiene after touching a patient’s immediate surroundings or equipment, even when the patient was not directly touched.
source_row.source_detail: Indications for hand hygiene, including after touching patient surroundings/equipment. Current CDC hand-hygiene guidance at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.source_name: CDC — Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_row.stem: A nurse enters a room, adjusts an IV pump in the patient’s immediate surroundings without touching the patient, and then leaves. When is hand hygiene indicated?
